titel: Hotel near Venlo city centre | Hotel Asteria Venray
omschrijving: Venlo city centre is a 24-minute drive from Hotel Asteria in Venray. Shopping, the Maasboulevard and the Markt, then wellness and dinner in the evening.
hero-sub: Shopping streets, the Maasboulevard and a terrace on the Markt, a 24-minute drive from your hotel room in Venray.
hero-alt: Venlo town hall with its two towers and the stone staircase on the Markt
oog-kop: Venlo city centre at a glance
t2-waarde: Q-Park Centrum Maasboulevard, Prinsessesingel 5, open 24 hours
t3-waarde: Tue to Sat from 10 am, Thursday until 9 pm
t4-waarde: Wednesday and Saturday on the Mgr. Nolensplein
v1-kop: A city centre on the Meuse
v1-p1: Venlo is a 24-minute drive from Hotel Asteria and, like Venray, sits on the Meuse (Maas). In the city centre you walk from the shopping streets down to the river and back up to the Markt, the main square, where the town hall from 1597 stands. Everything is close together, so the car can stay in the car park all day.
v1-p2: The familiar chains and fashion brands are in the Lomstraat, the Vleesstraat and along the Maasboulevard. If you prefer independent shops, wander into the Festina Lente streets: the Gasthuisstraat, the Jodenstraat and the Klaasstraat, with boutiques, specialist shops and delicatessens.
v1-alt: A red listed building with shops on the ground floor in Venlo city centre
v2-p1: On the river side of the city centre lies the Maasboulevard: shops, cafés, restaurants and homes right on the water. On a dry day you can sit on a terrace here looking out over the Meuse and the bridge.
v2-p2: Elsewhere in the centre you will also find terraces, cafés, lunch spots and restaurants. Take your time over a long lunch; dinner awaits in Venray in the evening.
v2-alt: Terraces on the Maasboulevard in Venlo looking out over the Meuse
v3-p1: The town hall with its two towers stands on the Markt, surrounded by cafés and terraces. Close to the station are the Limburgs Museum and Museum van Bommel van Dam, for modern art. To get to know the city better, pick up a leaflet for a self-guided walk at the tourist information point on the Keulsepoort.
v3-alt: Café Central with its terrace on the corner of the Markt and the Steenstraat in Venlo
tip: Going on a Saturday or Sunday? Until the end of 2026 you can park free of charge at Sint Urbanusweg 43, and a free shuttle bus takes you to the Maaskade every quarter of an hour. Please note: the gates there close at 8 pm. On weekdays, drive on to the car park on the Maasboulevard. And book a table in our brasserie before you set off.
g1-tekst: Monday from 1 pm, Tuesday to Saturday from 10 am. Thursday is late-night shopping until 9 pm, and on Sundays many shops are open from noon to 5 pm.
g1-alt: Shop buildings with bunting in the Lomstraat in Venlo
g2-tekst: There are seven Q-Park car parks around the city centre. The one on the Maasboulevard is open 24 hours and has 535 spaces.
g2-alt: Grassy bank of the Meuse with the bridge and the new buildings of the Maasboulevard in Venlo
g3-tekst: At Boekhandel Koops, a bookshop at Keulsepoort 12, also open on Sunday afternoons. This is where you pick up leaflets for a walk through the city.
g3-alt: The towers of Venlo town hall against a blue sky
g4-tekst: On Wednesdays from 9 am to 4 pm and on Saturdays from 8 am to 3 pm on the Mgr. Nolensplein.
g4-alt: Corn cobs with a price board on a market stall in Venlo
dag-kop: How to make a day of it
dag-sub: Breakfast at the hotel, into the city during the day and back to Venray in the late afternoon for the sauna and dinner.
m1-tekst: The breakfast buffet is served from 7 to 10 am on weekdays and from 8 to 10.30 am at weekends. Then it is a 24-minute drive to Venlo, just in time for the shops.
m1-alt: Breakfast buffet in the restaurant of Hotel Asteria
m2-tekst: Shop in the Lomstraat and the Festina Lente streets, stroll along the Meuse and have lunch on a terrace on the Markt. On Wednesdays and Saturdays there is also a market on the Mgr. Nolensplein.
m2-alt: The tower of the Sint-Martinuskerk above the rooftops of Venlo
m3-tekst: Back in Venray, warm up in the sauna. The wellness area is open Monday to Thursday from 4 pm to 10 pm and Friday to Sunday from noon to 10 pm. Tuesday is swimwear day.
m3-alt: Foot bath in the wellness area on the Top Floor
m4-tekst: End the day at a table in the hotel brasserie. The kitchen is open until 9.30 pm, and afterwards your room is just a lift ride away.
m4-alt: Bar in the brasserie of Hotel Asteria
kamers-kop: After the city, a night in Venray
kamers-sub: That way you do not have to drive home after dinner. Choose your room; you will see the price for your dates straight away when you book.
kaart-regel: Venlo lies south-east of Venray, on the Meuse. The map also shows three other days out near the hotel.
kaart-naam: Venlo city centre, Maasboulevard car park, Prinsessesingel 5, 5911 HS Venlo
kaart-alt: Map of North Limburg with Hotel Asteria in Venray, Venlo city centre and three other days out
f1-v: How far is Venlo city centre from Hotel Asteria?
f1-a: By car it is 26.5 kilometres, about 24 minutes to the car park on the Maasboulevard. Parking at Hotel Asteria is free, so you can simply leave the car outside until you check out.
f2-v: How much time do I need for Venlo?
f2-a: An afternoon is enough for shopping, a walk along the Meuse and lunch on the Markt. If you also want to visit a museum, allow a whole day. You will still be back in time for the sauna, as the wellness area is open until 10 pm.
f3-v: What can I do in Venlo when it rains?
f3-a: Then head for the shops, the cafés and the museums. The Limburgs Museum and Museum van Bommel van Dam are close to the station, within walking distance of the shopping streets.
f4-v: Where do I park in Venlo?
f4-a: There are seven Q-Park car parks around the city centre, including Centrum Maasboulevard at Prinsessesingel 5, open 24 hours. On Saturdays and Sundays until the end of 2026 you can park free of charge at Sint Urbanusweg 43; a free shuttle bus then runs to the Maaskade every quarter of an hour. On Saturdays the market takes over the car park on the Mgr. Nolensplein.
f5-v: Can I bring my dog to Venlo?
f5-a: Your dog is welcome to walk with you through the streets of the city centre. Whether it is also welcome in a shop, museum or café is up to each business.
f6-v: Can I still use the wellness area and have dinner at the hotel after Venlo?
f6-a: Yes. The wellness area is open Monday to Thursday from 4 pm to 10 pm and Friday to Sunday from noon to 10 pm. Tuesday is swimwear day. Dinner is served in the brasserie until 9.30 pm.

arcen.desc: Arcen is part of the municipality of Venlo and lies a quarter of an hour's drive north of the city centre. Around the 17th-century castle are the Kasteeltuinen Arcen (the castle gardens), more than fifteen gardens ranging from a rose garden and an Oriental water garden to the tropical glasshouse Casa Verde. The gardens are closed in winter.
arcen.credit: Photos: Vincent van Zeijst and Kasteeltuinen Arcen via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.

hertogjan.desc: Arcen is home to the Hertog Jan brewery. A guide takes you through the brewing process, from hops and malt to tasting the beer. Book the tour in advance; expect narrow corridors and 144 steps. The Kasteeltuinen are in the same village.
hertogjan.credit: Photos: B. Hulshoff and Steven Lek via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.

maasduinen.desc: Along the east bank of the Meuse, towards the German border, lies a strip of river dunes covering more than 4,500 hectares of woodland, heath, drift sand and fens. You will find routes at the visitor centre in Well. The park is closer to the hotel than Venlo, so it fits nicely into a second day.
maasduinen.credit: Photos: Lieblingsgouda, Steven Lek, Carelbullens and Jonathation via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA), cropped.
